p: Manor Wildlife Park has had a bit of telly fame of its own. It's owned by Anna Ryder Richardson, the interior designer best known from Changing Rooms, who took it on with her family in the late 2000s. Since then it's built a reputation as a friendly, hands-on wildlife park that's a fixture on many a Pembrokeshire holiday itinerary.

Tenby is a holiday hotspot, so on sunny days in August you'll want to arrive earlier to avoid the busiest spells. On rainier days, expect plenty of families with the same idea. Allow a good few hours, catch any talks that appeal, and make use of the play spots between animal areas when the kids need a break. A picnic on a fine day keeps costs down and gives everyone a breather.

South Pembrokeshire is a goldmine of family days out. Folly Farm, near Begelly, mixes a zoo, a farm and a vintage funfair under one roof. Oakwood, close to Narberth, is a theme park with rides for thrill-seekers and smaller ones for younger visitors. Heatherton World of Activities, right on the doorstep near St Florence, offers everything from crazy golf to paintball and karting. Back in Tenby, the town museum and art gallery tells the story of the area, and the Pembrokeshire Coast Path passes nearby for stunning clifftop walks. Saundersfoot, just along the coast, has a sandy harbour beach and a good choice of cafes. Carew Castle, a short drive west, sits beside a tidal millpond and makes a dramatic final stop on the way back from a day of animals and beaches.
